short: Switzerland has no AI act. The Federal Council decided on 12 February 2025 to ratify the Council of Europe AI convention through targeted, mostly sectoral amendments; the consultation draft is not yet published, and the revised data protection act binds.
title: Switzerland AI Laws
subtitle: No AI act: sectoral amendments planned, the data protection act binds
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act. On 12 February 2025 the Federal Council decided against a horizontal AI law. It chose to ratify the Council of Europe's Framework Convention on AI and to amend Swiss law where needed, mostly sector by sector, with cross-cutting changes limited to areas such as transparency, data protection, non-discrimination and supervision. The Federal Office of Justice is preparing the consultation draft; the Federal Council's planning extract for 2027, which states that it has no official character, places the opening of the consultation in the first half of 2027. Until then the binding layer is the revised Federal Act on Data Protection. Verified on 25 October 2026 against admin.ch, the Federal Office of Justice and Fedlex.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateLegal force
Federal Council decision on regulating AIPress release12 February 2025Policy decision
Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP, DSG)SR 235.1In force 1 September 2023Binding

Who regulates and enforces

  • Federal Office of Justice, Federal Department of Justice and Police: leads the AI amendments.
  • Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC): supervises the FADP and files criminal complaints (art. 65(2)).
  • Cantonal prosecutors: prosecute FADP offences (art. 65(1)).

Scope and reach

The FADP applies to facts "die sich in der Schweiz auswirken, auch wenn sie im Ausland veranlasst werden": those that have effects in Switzerland, even if caused abroad (art. 3(1)).

Core obligations

  • No AI-specific obligations yet. The FADP's duties apply to any AI processing personal data.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Breaches of the duties to inform and disclose, of the duty of care, of professional secrecy, or of FDPIC ordersA fine of up to CHF 250,000, on the responsible private person; the business may pay instead where the fine is no more than CHF 50,000 (art. 64(2))FADP arts. 60 to 63Cantonal prosecutors

What is coming next

  • First half of 2027: the Federal Council's target for opening the consultation on accession to the Council of Europe convention and the related amendments, per its planning extract (target date 30 June 2027).

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the date Switzerland signed the Council of Europe convention, because the Federal Council's release announcing it is written in the future tense and the treaty office could not be read.
